title: DET-25-01 query result — OpenProcessApiCall match against lsass.exe
event_type: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Advanced Hunting, DeviceEvents table, ActionType = OpenProcessApiCall (result row from the §7.2 base query)

callouts.explanation: The comsvcs.dll MiniDump invocation is the exact Detection Test action from §7.2 — this full command line is what lets an analyst distinguish a deliberate LSASS dump from a benign process-access event, since InitiatingProcessFileName alone (rundll32.exe) is an extremely common LOLBin.

This value must be extracted via parse_json(AdditionalFields).GrantedAccess per the base query's extend step; §7.2 flags this extraction as unverified against a live tenant schema, unlike the Sysmon GrantedAccess value list in Part 24.

This is the field the base query's allowlist filters on (InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("wmiprvse.exe", "svchost.exe", "MsMpEng.exe")); the Blind Spot box in §7.2 notes this match is on name alone, with no path or hash check.

Confirms the accessed target is lsass.exe itself (matched case-insensitively via =~ in the base query), the field that scopes the whole query to LSASS-specific access rather than any process-access event.

note: Illustrative and conceptual only — this represents what a matching DeviceEvents row would look like in the Defender Advanced Hunting result grid; it is not a captured product screenshot, since this book's available lab evidence has no Defender for Endpoint-onboarded host.
